Note: The runner lists permission sets with a blank Name; real BC lists none blank, measured upstream on 27.0-28.4 in StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#91. MEASURED ROOT CAUSE, not inferred: 167 of the 461 permission sets across the platform apps the runner loads declare no Caption at all (Base Application 7 of 258, including LOCAL id 1001; System Application 128 of 164; System.app 23 of 25; Business Foundation 9 of 14). For System.app's 23 this is confirmed twice over -- their SymbolReference.json entries carry only Assignable and IncludedPermissionSets (no Caption, no CaptionML), and their own AL source shipped inside the .app under src/Permissions/*.permissionset.al declares no Caption either. So the runner reads the symbol data CORRECTLY and BuildMetadataPermissionSetValue's `permissionSet.Caption ?? string.Empty` faithfully reproduces what those apps state; the caption real BC shows comes from somewhere the .app does not state. NOTE for anyone re-measuring: most platform .app files are R2R wrappers whose payload is a NESTED .app, and SymbolReference.json lives inside the nested one -- a scan that does not recurse finds only System.app's 25 and misses LOCAL entirely. WHAT IS NOT YET MEASURED, and why this is a known gap rather than a fix: what BC actually puts in Name for a permission set declaring no Caption. Substituting the Role ID would make this test pass, but no service tier has been asked whether that is what BC does, and the upstream test deliberately declines to assert the mechanism ('Either BC substitutes something (the Role ID) ... or every permission set in a stock installation happens to declare one. No service tier has been asked to distinguish those, so neither is asserted here.'). This measurement rules out the second branch but not the first. Corpus PR #102 is the diagnostic that reads LOCAL's Name off real BC on all 8 legs and settles it. The other 7 tests in codeunit 60290 pass here. Tracked as #2388; the fix removes this entry.
